models_evaluated: deep learning caries lesion segmentation models trained on ACTA-DIRECT dataset

links.outcome: AI caries segmentation accuracy under independent micro-CT reference versus training-matched annotations
links.effect: No significant difference among models against micro-CT annotations; accuracy was significantly higher when evaluated with training-matched annotations, indicating evaluation bias from non-independent reference standards.
links.quote: However, the diagnostic accuracy was considered statistically significantly higher when the results of the AI models were evaluated with the training-matched annotations.

unlisted_practices: Comparing single-dentist, aggregated (majority vote, consensus, STAPLE), and micro-CT-based annotation strategies for model training

screen.reason: The study empirically tests how the choice of evaluation reference standard (micro-CT vs training-matched annotations) impacts the assessed accuracy of diagnostic AI models, directly addressing validation practices.
